result.title: Autoregressive Multimodal Anomaly Detection with Large Language Models for Microservice Systems
result.summary: Microservice systems have become a dominant architecture for large-scale cloud applications, enabling rapid deployment and elastic scaling. However, ensuring the reliability and availability of microservice systems critically relies on effective anomaly detection, as failures and performance anomalies can quickly propagate across services and severely impact end-to-end system behavior. Existing multimodal anomaly detection approaches for microservice systems often struggle with two fundamental limitations: (i) the neglect of modality-specific characteristics in favor of cross-modality fusion, and (ii) the "identity-shortcut" problem that affects the feature reconstruction process. To address these issues, we propose LLMMAD, an autoregressive multimodal anomaly detection framework for microservice systems based on Large Language Models (LLMs). Initially, to reconcile cross-modality fusion with modality-specific preservation, LLMMAD embeds and recombines multimodal data into a unified sequence for LLM processing to model inter-modality relationships, while employing modality-wise reconstruction heads to retain modality-specific information. Subsequently, to eliminate the identity-shortcut, we implement a prediction-driven autoregressive objective, under which the model predicts future states rather than copies current inputs. Finally, we conduct extensive experiments on three real-world datasets. The results demonstrate that LLMMAD consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods, achieving F1-score improvements of 3.1%, 1.4%, and 0.9%, respectively, thereby providing a more reliable solution for microservice monitoring.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 LLMMAD，把微服务的多模态监控数据嵌入重排为统一序列交由 LLM 自回归建模，并用模态专属重建头保留模态特性、以预测未来状态的目标替代重建以缓解「identity-shortcut」问题。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「重建目标易退化为复制输入」的 identity-shortcut 分析及改为预测后续状态的做法，可能与 latent 状态信息坍缩、视觉旁路等训练监督问题可比，可供核查；但任务本身是微服务异常检测，不涉及视觉推理。
